## 固定收益開篇論點

美國服務業成長放緩、供應鏈壓力減輕，進一步壓低市場對聯準會近期升息的預期，帶動美國公債在7月6日小幅上漲；但服務業就業改善、投入成本仍高，使各年期公債未能全面大漲。2年期殖利率下跌2.6個基點至4.112%，5年期下降3個基點至4.201%，10年期回落1.5個基點至4.47%；30年期則幾乎持平於4.985%。殖利率曲線因而趨陡，2年與10年期利差擴大1.1個基點至35.8個基點，2年與30年期利差增加2.5個基點至87.3個基點。

這波行情主要來自實質利率下滑，而非通膨補償回落。10年期實質殖利率下跌2.7個基點至2.219%，10年期損益兩平通膨率反而上升1.2個基點至2.251%。6月ISM服務業PMI由54.5降至54.0，商業活動與新訂單放緩，但就業重返擴張，價格指數雖由71.3回落，仍高達67.7。紐約聯準銀行供應鏈指數則由修正後高於歷史平均1.81個標準差，降至高於平均1.25個標準差，顯示物流壓力正在緩解，但尚未恢復正常。

能源帶來更強的通膨降溫動能。荷莫茲海峽受干擾而延誤的原油重新流入市場後，沙烏地阿美將8月銷往亞洲的阿拉伯輕原油價格每桶下調$11，降至較區域基準低$1.50，為至少自2000年以來最大單月降幅。WTI收跌0.20%至$68.55，近一個月累計下跌24.29%；布蘭特原油當日上漲0.26%至$71.99，但月跌幅仍達22.67%。近月原油價格重挫，降低眼前的能源風險；然而損益兩平通膨率小幅上升，顯示投資人並未把單一交易日的油價訊號，視為足以化解服務業及生產者價格壓力的完整答案。

聯準會官員的發言也延續這份謹慎。理事Christopher Waller反駁主席Kevin Warsh傾向淡化前瞻指引的立場，主張只要運用方式保持彈性，前瞻指引仍是有用的政策工具，但未提出新的利率時程。市場評論顯示，6月非農就業報告疲弱後，交易員已降低7月升息機率，卻仍反映今年至少升息一次的可能性。升息時點延後有利於短天期美國公債；長端則持續受到通膨不確定性及本週附息債供給的制約。

風險資產表現穩健，並未轉向防禦。標普500指數上漲0.72%，那斯達克100指數上升1.26%，費城半導體指數在連跌兩個交易日後反彈2.17%。高收益債與新興市場債基金小幅走高，投資級債ETF LQD則近乎持平。這組合顯示，美國公債行情反映的是政策時點調整，而非資金逃離成長或信用風險。

## 服務業數據改變聯準會風險時點，而非方向

6月服務業報告延續非農就業公布後的偏弱基調，但並未顯示美國經濟最大部門已接近萎縮。ISM整體指數下降0.5點至54.0，仍是連續第24個月擴張；商業活動指數由57.7降至55.4，新訂單由57.3降至55.1。兩者仍明顯高於50的榮枯線，表示需求雖然動能放緩，仍持續成長。

就業是鴿派解讀的主要制衡因素。就業指數由47.9升至51.2，從萎縮轉為擴張。這項改善並未推翻6月非農就業疲弱的結果，卻提供另一項獨立指標，顯示服務業者並非普遍削減勞動需求。對聯準會而言，產出、訂單與聘僱未同步強勁，使政策急迫性較低；但三項指標也未全面惡化，經濟仍比全面轉弱的情境更具韌性。

價格壓力仍然可觀。服務業價格指數由71.3降至67.7，較5月高點明顯回落，但仍反映投入成本普遍上升。供應商交貨指數也由55.2降至54.4。整體數據僅呈邊際改善，尚未出現足以終結2026年稍後是否再次升息之爭的低通膨讀數。

供應鏈報告進一步支持部分商品與物流壓力正在消退的判斷。紐約聯準銀行全球供應鏈壓力指數6月由5月修正後的1.810降至1.249，相當於高於歷史平均1.25個標準差。該指數綜合7個相互連結經濟體的運輸成本與製造業指標。指數下降顯示交貨與運費壓力不再如此極端，因而攸關生產者與商品通膨；但讀數仍為正值，也表示供給狀況依然比正常時期緊張。

這項差異可解釋實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率的分歧。10年期名目殖利率下跌1.5個基點，實質殖利率下降2.7個基點，通膨補償卻增加1.2個基點。服務業活動放緩與物流壓力下降，降低投資人要求的實質利率負擔；就業改善及仍高的服務業價格指數，則使通膨預期未同步下滑。受能源價格更大幅度反轉影響，10年期損益兩平通膨率近一個月仍下降11.8個基點，實質殖利率同期則上升5.7個基點。

Waller的談話重點在於聯準會如何於這些交錯訊號下溝通，而非下一步應採取哪項決策。他在羅馬舉行的義大利央行會議上表示，疫情期間通膨急升時，前瞻指引曾在實際升息前協助收緊金融情勢。他也承認，官員有時過於僵化，例如2020及2021年通膨加速之際，仍曾釋出利率會維持不變的訊號。

這與Warsh承諾採取更依賴數據、較少倚重未來政策路徑指引的立場，在著重點上有所不同。Waller認為，只要新資訊改變後，指引不至於綁住官員原先承諾的政策路徑，前瞻指引仍有價值。最新數據正呈現這類使無條件訊號格外危險的交錯力量：服務業需求放緩、就業面改善、物流壓力減輕，但投入成本仍高。

聯準會6月維持目標利率區間不變，18名官員中有9人預測今年至少升息一次，Warsh則未提交利率預測。Waller並未利用週一的場合支持或否定這些預測，因此不應把其發言視為另一項利率訊號。其意義在於延續一場制度層面的辯論：附帶條件的溝通能否在不限制委員會因應新資訊的前提下影響金融情勢。

市場定價仍反映殘餘升息風險。一份盤中觀察顯示，交換市場交易員認為下次會議升息的機率約為25%，高於疲弱非農就業報告公布後立即反映的水準，但低於報告公布前約三分之一的機率。更廣泛的匯市報導也顯示，交易員仍預期聯準會2026年至少升息一次。這些證據指向升息情境遭到延後且不確定性增加，而非徹底消失。

市場恢復全日交易後，美國公債交投活躍。FINRA記錄到311,879筆交易，面額成交量達$9,138億，較7月2日縮短交易時段增加7.7%。名目附息債成交量增加2.6%至$6,516億，TIPS成交量則增加13.1%至$173億。這些數字反映雙向成交而非投資人方向，但顯示本次小幅上漲發生於假期後交易活動回升之際。

現金需求也吸收了$1,710億國庫券供給。財政部標售$920億91天期國庫券，最高得標利率為3.735%，投標倍數2.58倍。競爭性投標總額為$2,338.13億，其中接受$886.31億；間接投標人獲配$429.88億、直接投標人$68.41億、主要交易商$388.02億。這批國庫券於7月9日交割、10月8日到期。

$790億182天期國庫券標售的最高得標利率為3.830%，投標倍數3.05倍。競爭性投標總額$2,380.19億，其中接受$764.55億；間接投標人獲配$457.54億、直接投標人$73.46億、主要交易商$233.56億。最高利率的配售比例僅0.86%，相較之下，91天期標售為93.49%。由於缺少發行前交易水準，這些結果只能確認投標覆蓋程度與配售情況，無法判斷標售是否優於市價或出現尾差；不過，大規模假期後國庫券供給仍在7月9日交割前順利消化，未見明顯融資干擾。

## 油價下跌，歐洲管線通膨壓力仍在

沙烏地阿拉伯大幅調降售價，為近月原油供給過剩提供實質證據，也使全球利率市場的爭論更加複雜，因為央行官員仍持續警告通膨的遞延效應。沙烏地阿美將8月銷往亞洲的阿拉伯輕原油官方售價每桶下調$11，降至較區域基準低$1.50。這是至少26年來最大單月降幅，背景是荷莫茲海峽周邊交通受干擾期間受困或延誤的原油重新釋出。

這項折價並未被描述為新一輪市占率爭奪戰。能源分析師認為，海峽交通不均衡地恢復正常、波斯灣產油國重建供應流量，造成暫時性庫存壓力；沙烏地阿拉伯也依OPEC+協議溫和提高供給配額。對債市的立即影響有利於通膨降溫，但效果的規模與持續時間，取決於延誤船貨消化後是否仍有過剩供給。

歐洲數據則顯示，現貨能源降價不會自動消除仍在傳導途中的通膨。歐元區工業生產者價格5月上漲0.2%，4月增幅修正為0.7%；歐盟價格同樣上漲0.2%，4月增幅修正為0.8%。歐元區能源價格單月下跌1.0%，但不含能源的生產者價格上升0.7%。與一年前相比，歐元區整體價格上漲5.9%，不含能源價格增加2.8%；能源價格即使單月下降，仍比一年前高14.0%。

歐洲央行執行委員Isabel Schnabel強調現貨價格紓緩與累積衝擊之間的落差。她表示，中東脆弱的和平局勢帶動油價迅速下跌，但市場尚未回到戰前狀態，天然氣價格仍比衝突前高約40%。她也警告，能源庫存仍需補充，核心通膨動能也比整體通膨率降幅所顯示的更強。

Schnabel另指出，歐洲熱浪、萊茵河低水位及AI投資需求都構成額外風險。她擔心，即使原油維持在戰時高點之下，能源、運輸及供應鏈效應仍可能傳導至食品、服務與工資。5月生產者價格結構部分支持這項保留：能源項目單月下降，非能源價格卻持續上升。

比利時央行總裁Pierre Wunsch在同一場合提出較不鷹派的評估。他表示，整體環境已明顯平靜，仍可考慮再次升息；但若原始衝擊消退且未引發顯著第二輪效應，就不需要大幅收緊政策。他尤其認為工資走勢溫和。Wunsch與Schnabel的分歧已不在能源情勢是否改善，而在先前衝擊是否已轉化為足以要求另一次政策回應的壓力。

經濟活動為通膨疑慮提供些許抵銷。德國5月實質製造業訂單上升1.9%；4月降幅則由初報的3.8%修正為3.2%。其他運輸設備訂單激增85.0%，對整體數字影響很大。排除大型合約後，訂單仍增加1.0%，基礎表現較為穩健；但3月至5月總訂單仍較之前三個月低0.2%。

各地區需求表現不一。來自歐元區的訂單增加11.2%，貨幣聯盟以外的需求則下降3.2%。這份數據顯示訂單明顯反彈，且歐洲需求成分較強，但並不代表德國工業景氣全面加速。

歐元區零售量5月上升0.2%，4月降幅修正為0.3%；歐盟零售量增加0.5%，4月降幅修正為0.6%。歐元區食品、飲料與菸草銷售量增加0.6%，非食品銷售量微升0.1%；汽車燃料銷售量單月下降0.5%，年減4.6%。歐元區整體零售量較一年前增加1.6%，歐盟則年增1.9%。這是由食品帶動的溫和復甦，而非消費全面加速。

上述數據使歐洲公債同時面對兩項現況：成長數據已非全面疲弱，通膨動能也愈來愈不只集中於當前能源價格。停火及油價下跌後，交易員已降低歐洲央行進一步升息的預期；Schnabel的警告及堅挺的非能源生產者價格支持保持謹慎，Wunsch對溫和工資與原始衝擊消退的著重，則支持等待第二輪效應的證據。

## 初級市場獎勵規模、改革與資產負債表修復

企業與主權借款人都遇到具承接力的初級市場，但各筆交易也劃出清楚界線：能展現改革成效、以擔保品支持再融資，或具備強勁指標券需求的發行人獲得資金，市場定價仍不具經濟效益的借款人則選擇觀望。

Welltower將原訂加拿大幣交易規模提高至C$11.5億，比最初尋求的最低C$7億高逾60%。這家美國高齡住宅營運商發行C$7.5億5年期債券及C$4億7年期債券。較長年期券由36名買方提交的訂單超過發行規模3倍，最終定價較加拿大公債高93個基點，比初步討論水準收窄2個基點。募集資金將用於一般企業用途，包括償債。這筆交易進一步推高美國借款人的加拿大幣發行紀錄，並顯示跨境需求足以同時支持擴大規模與小幅改善定價。

瑞典債務催收公司Intrum先前因融資成本上升而被迫重整，如今首次重返歐洲高收益債市場。公司尋求發行€5.25億、2031年到期的優先擔保債券，募集資金擬用於贖回2027年到期的歐元及瑞典克朗擔保債券。Intrum在重新安排到期日後，已於去年退出美國《破產法》第11章程序。

這筆擬議債券承接一項75億瑞典克朗的股權資本計畫，目標是把去槓桿進度提前約兩年。Intrum表示，計畫中的現金增資部分已全數獲認購，扣除成本前將籌得60億瑞典克朗。新股本與擔保再融資的組合，與無擔保重返一般融資市場有實質差異：交易依靠資本結構改善與擔保品，同時延後2027年到期債務。

TenneT Germany在完成新的股權結構後，籌備首次發債；新股東包括德國政府、荷蘭退休金資本與主權投資人。這家電網營運商就一筆分成4期、期限橫跨4至20年的歐元歐洲綠色債券交易召開投資人會議。隨再生能源發電及資料中心需求加重輸電基礎設施負擔，公司計畫投資€670億於德國電網，2026年至2030年平均每年約投入€130億。

德國政府取得TenneT Germany 25.1%的股權，荷蘭退休基金APG、新加坡GIC及挪威央行投資管理公司合計持有約46%，前母公司TenneT Holding保留28.9%。穆迪給予公司Baa1、展望穩定的評等，標普與惠譽均評為BBB+、展望穩定；擬發行債券的預期評等也大致落在相同水準。全球公用事業上半年發債已超過$3,370億，這項融資進一步顯示，電網擴建與電力需求正轉化為持續的資本市場借款。

Péter Magyar於4月終結Viktor Orbán長達16年的統治後，匈牙利完成€30億主權債發售，也是政權更迭後首次國際發債。債務管理機構分別發行€15億2032年及2037年到期債券，合計訂單超過€80億。較短年期券定價為中期交換利率加80個基點，較長年期券為加125個基點，兩者均較初步指引收窄35個基點。

匈牙利重新取得歐盟資金，加上政府承諾採用歐元，已帶動債券收斂行情，本次交易將這波漲勢轉化為融資成果。匈牙利2035年到期既有歐元債的殖利率，已由3月高點下降近2個百分點至3.94%。然而，新政府指稱前朝低報支出後，目前仍面臨預算赤字大幅超標。Generali策略師Guillaume Tresca認為，多數債券漲勢已經發生，並表示匈牙利今年稍後可能再發行美元債。這次交易的強勁表現驗證市場對新政治方向的需求，但尚未解決加入歐元區所需的財政工作。

阿根廷做出相反的融資選擇。經濟部長Luis Caputo表示，政府不打算在2026或2027年發行國際債券，只有市場借款成本能與較便宜的替代方案競爭時才會回歸。惠譽與標普近期把阿根廷評等由CCC級別調升至B-，6月升評後，其債券相對美國公債的利差收窄近80個基點；即便如此，指標2035年債券殖利率仍約為8.6%。

Caputo以一筆世界銀行擔保、規模$20億的融資利率6.3%，作為評估市場融資的最低比較基準，但拒絕提出確切的發債門檻。政府計畫主要仰賴國內美元計價發行，支應2026年剩餘期間及明年約$250億美元債務服務。今年迄今已在國內籌得約$40億，預計年底前再籌$20億、2027年籌得$50億，近期也以接近7.5%的利率為一筆$60億附買回協議再融資。官員預期2026年融資計畫可產生$37億盈餘，並可結轉至明年。

阿根廷的目標是在Milei可能的第2個任期結束前，也就是2031年，取得投資級評等。Caputo表示，3大信評機構中有2家認為這條路徑可行。目前的決策範圍較窄：近期利差收窄改善了市場融資條件，但幅度仍不足以取代有擔保或國內替代方案。

亞洲境外市場則提供更廣泛的結構性融資訊號。截至6月30日止一季，區內借款人發行等值創紀錄$1,540億的美元及歐元債券。日本發行人占約40%，扭轉先前由中國企業主導市場的局面。日本借款人發行約$620億，相較之下，澳洲約$260億，中國約$200億。

日本國內殖利率升高，使能把募集資金換回日圓的借款人更偏好外幣發債。亞太借款人的歐元債發行量增加63%，創下單季約€370億的紀錄，占美元與歐元合計發行量28%，高於2021年上一次區域高峰時的8%。花旗集團預期，排除日本國內交易後，今年美元、歐元與日圓發行量將增加約10%至$4,750億。超過5%的高評級企業債殖利率持續支撐需求，但亞洲新興市場投資級美元債利差約55個基點，面對通膨或地緣政治波動再起時的緩衝空間有限。

## 新興市場的美元與本地融資交易分歧

美元整體部位所反映的鷹派程度，遠高於7月6日近乎持平的收盤表現。截至6月30日，押注美元走強的期貨部位接近$400億，創逾10年最大規模；美元6月上漲2%。美元指數週一收於100.85，單日跌幅不到0.01%，一週下跌0.26%，但近一個月仍上漲0.78%。

這些部位反映市場預期，即使疲弱非農就業使可能升息的時點延後，聯準會的緊縮程度仍可能高於其他主要央行，也使融資選擇對新興市場愈發重要。美元重新走強已侵蝕部分本幣資產漲幅；聯準會若再次升息，也會縮小支撐利差交易的殖利率優勢。最新美國數據減輕了眼前風險，卻未消除根本的利差。

日圓最清楚地反映這項利差。高盛以日本財政壓力、美國公債殖利率將長期維持高檔，以及日本央行只會漸進升息為由，把12個月美元兌日圓預測由155上調至165，並預測3個月為162、6個月為163，也偏好以日圓作為利差交易的融資貨幣。選擇權市場反映美元兌日圓在翌年6月前升至165的機率約為76%。

日本前外匯官員Tatsuo Yamasaki則持相反看法，估計日圓至少被低估10%，合理水準可能接近130日圓兌1美元。他預期日本央行會進一步升息，並認為即使聯準會再有動作，也可能只是一次性升息，因此利差進一步擴大的空間有限。他還警告，日本財務省已不只停留在口頭警告，可能採取規模較小、較不易察覺的干預行動，擾亂日圓空頭部位；不過，他認為日本與美國聯手干預的可能性不高。

這場爭論呈現兩種不同時間尺度。當前融資條件與相對政策利率仍有利於日圓融資部位；但日圓低估幅度與干預風險，也提高了押注日圓將平順貶值的成本。美國收盤前後，日圓接近162兌1美元，避險基金的看空程度則升至2007年以來最高。

菲律賓央行總裁Eli Remolona提出另一項政策訊號，表示經濟可以承受再升息25個基點。通膨遠高於3%目標之際，菲律賓央行今年已升息50個基點。Remolona表示，8月27日會議仍可能再次升息；但只要通膨預期維持穩定，官員不傾向採取更大幅度的調升。

他的成長條件十分明確。Remolona預期經濟活動將於下半年回升，並希望GDP成長超過3%；先前公共工程專案受到審查，拖慢核准進度，政府支出若復甦可提供支持。6月通膨排定在他發言後公布，市場預期將由5月的6.8%降至6.5%。總裁的說法因此保留溫和升息的可能性，同時把經濟承受升息的能力，繫於財政執行改善及下半年成長增強。

印度銀行體系顯示，官方融資措施即使不調整政策利率，也能改變國內發行。銀行在截至7月2日的3個交易日內未發行任何定存單；6月16日至29日曾籌得7,080億盧比，也低於6月上半月約1兆盧比。發行放緩前，印度央行決定負擔銀行在海外籌措美元時的避險成本，預期可吸引逾$500億外幣存款。

1年期定存單利率由5月逾兩年高點7.96%降至6.84%。銀行財務主管預期，隨銀行以存續較長的外幣存款取代昂貴的短期融資，發行量在8月或9月前將維持低檔。CSB Bank的Alok Singh表示，定存單利率可能再下降20至25個基點；但印度央行若積極收回流動性，效果將相反。

智利則提供一項較長期的例子，顯示外國需求如何回應匯率水準、降息預期及政權更迭。非居民持有的披索主權債5月創紀錄增加$29.3億至$202億，使年初以來增幅達36%。資金流入發生在José Antonio Kast當選後，其政策提案包括調降企業稅、提供投資保證及就業補貼。

智利1年期損益兩平通膨率自5月初以來下降逾200個基點至2.33%，低於央行3%的目標。交換市場反映一年後政策利率為4.26%，較前一個月下降40個基點，也低於目前4.5%的基準利率。財政風險限制了收斂空間：政府已放棄在2030年前實現結構性預算平衡的目標，目前設定相當於GDP 1.5%的赤字，並請求授權今年再發行$62億債券。創紀錄外資流入反映政治與利率預期改善，但能否持續，仍取決於財政整頓能否落實。

## 後續市場意義

下一個美國交易日將於7月7日美東時間08:30公布5月國際貿易數據，紐約聯準銀行則於11:00公布6月消費者預期調查。貿易流量將更新第2季成長追蹤；家庭對通膨、勞動市場及信用的預期，則可檢驗油價下跌與供應鏈壓力減輕，是否像改變近期聯準會定價一樣清楚地改變了民眾展望。

財政部接著於美東時間11:30標售$900億42天期國庫券及$520億364天期國庫券，13:00再標售$580億3年期公債。6月非農就業及服務業數據降低7月升息急迫性後，這次附息債標售是市場久期需求的首次直接考驗。評估結果時，需要觀察公布的最高得標殖利率、發行前交易參考水準及投標人配售，而不能只依據週一國庫券標售的強勁投標倍數。

主要政策事件是7月8日美東時間14:00公布6月16至17日FOMC會議紀錄。紀錄可顯示官員對2026年可能升息的轉向獲得多廣泛支持、如何權衡通膨與勞動市場韌性，以及在Warsh著手減少政策訊號前，Waller偏好的彈性前瞻指引得到多少支持。由於該次會議早於疲弱的6月非農就業報告及週一服務業數據，紀錄呈現的將是委員會的反應函數，而非對最新證據的回應。

同日美東時間13:00將增額發行$390億、票面利率4.375%的10年期公債。7月6日10年期殖利率僅下跌1.5個基點，且一週仍上升9.4個基點，本次標售將測試指標年期的久期需求。發債週期於7月9日以增額發行$220億、票面利率5.000%的30年期公債作結，兩批附息債均於7月15日交割。長債幾乎未參與週一漲勢，2年與30年期利差又擴大至87.3個基點，因此30年期標售尤其重要。

截至7月4日當週的初領失業救濟金人數，將在長債標售前公布。假期效應可能使數據雜訊較高，但仍能即時檢驗：非農就業放緩與ISM服務業就業改善，是否能在裁員未全面增加的情況下同時成立。

歐洲眼前的硬數據考驗，是7月7日美東時間02:00公布的德國5月工業生產。數據將顯示製造業訂單反彈1.9%，其中排除大型合約後增加1.0%，是否已轉化為當期產出。歐盟統計局接著於05:00公布4月服務業生產報告，為與持續工資及價格壓力最相關的經濟部門補充證據。

紐西蘭央行將於7月8日紐西蘭時間14:00公布7月政策決定，相當於美東時間7月7日22:00。5月決策後，官方現金利率為2.25%。這是本週亞太地區最重要的利率催化事件，將檢驗官員如何在國內需求與全球政策利率路徑轉向更高之間取得平衡。

日本下一批政策證據包括7月8日公布的日本央行放款與存款趨勢及第1季直接投資數據，央行並於7月9日發布地區經濟報告。報告對經濟活動、工資及價格的區域評估，將直接影響兩派觀點之爭：一方預期日圓將逐步走弱，另一方則是相信日本央行進一步升息能扭轉日圓低估的前官員。

油價仍是上述決策的共同條件。沙烏地阿拉伯降價及荷莫茲海峽交通恢復，加強了近期通膨降溫效果；但歐洲生產者價格與Schnabel的警告顯示，累積衝擊尚未從非能源成本中消失。原油若持續供過於求，各國央行將有更多時間分辨仍在傳導的價格壓力，是否會演變成持久的第二輪通膨；航運正常化若逆轉，輸入性價格風險則會迅速回升，而7月6日美國公債漲勢只消除了其中一部分。

overall_summary.headline: 服務業轉弱延後聯準會升息風險，美國公債小幅上漲，長端落後
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國公債7月6日小幅上漲，漲勢集中於短、中天期。2年期殖利率下跌2.6個基點至4.112%，5年期下降3個基點至4.201%，10年期回落1.5個基點至4.47%，30年期則幾乎持平於4.985%。2年與10年期利差擴大至35.8個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大至87.3個基點。10年期實質殖利率下跌2.7個基點，但損益兩平通膨率上升1.2個基點，顯示這波漲勢來自實質利率壓力降低，而非通膨補償全面退潮。

6月ISM服務業指數降至54.0，商業活動與新訂單放緩；紐約聯準銀行供應鏈指數則降至高於歷史平均1.25個標準差。就業重返擴張，服務業價格指數仍處於67.7的高檔，因此即使疲弱非農就業與活動轉弱降低7月升息的急迫性，2026年稍後再次升息的可能性依然存在。沙烏地阿美罕見大幅調降8月原油售價，加上原油價格月線重挫，帶來更強的近期通膨降溫訊號；然而服務業成本居高不下、歐洲非能源生產者通膨持續，使長端仍保持謹慎。

科技與半導體股領漲，股市走高；高收益債與新興市場債轉強，投資級信用債則近乎持平。這組合顯示市場正在調整政策時點，而非逃離成長或信用風險。初級市場也願意承接能提出規模、改革、擔保再融資或策略性投資的借款人；阿根廷則認為，即使近期利差已收窄，外部借款成本仍然過高。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries rallied modestly on July 6 as slower U.S. services growth and easing supply-chain pressure reinforced the retreat in near-term Federal Reserve tightening expectations, but improving services employment and still-high input costs prevented the move from becoming a broad duration surge. The 2-year yield fell 2.6 basis points to 4.112%, the 5-year declined 3 basis points to 4.201%, and the 10-year eased 1.5 basis points to 4.47%. The 30-year yield was almost unchanged at 4.985%, leaving the curve steeper: 2s10s widened 1.1 basis points to 35.8 basis points and 2s30s increased 2.5 basis points to 87.3 basis points.

The composition was more favorable to real duration than to inflation compensation. The 10-year real yield fell 2.7 basis points to 2.219%, while the 10-year breakeven rose 1.2 basis points to 2.251%. June’s ISM Services PMI slipped to 54.0 from 54.5, with business activity and new orders slowing, but employment returned to expansion and the prices index remained elevated at 67.7 even after retreating from 71.3. The New York Fed’s supply-chain index dropped to 1.25 standard deviations above its historical average from a revised 1.81, providing evidence that logistics stress was easing without yet returning to normal.

Energy supplied a stronger disinflationary impulse. Saudi Aramco cut the August price of Arab Light crude for Asian buyers by $11 a barrel to $1.50 below the regional benchmark, the largest monthly reduction since at least 2000, as barrels delayed by disruption in the Strait of Hormuz returned to the market. WTI settled 0.20% lower at $68.55 and was down 24.29% over one month. Brent rose 0.26% on the day to $71.99 but remained 22.67% lower over the month. The collapse in prompt crude prices reduced the immediate energy threat, although the small increase in breakevens showed that investors were not treating one session’s oil signal as a complete answer to persistent services and producer-price pressure.

Federal Reserve communication preserved that caution. Governor Christopher Waller defended forward guidance as a useful policy instrument when applied flexibly, pushing back against Chair Kevin Warsh’s preference to move away from it, but he offered no new rate timetable. Market commentary indicated that traders had reduced the probability of a July increase after the weak June payroll report, even as they continued to price at least one increase this year. Shorter Treasuries benefited from the delayed timetable; the long end remained constrained by inflation uncertainty and a week of coupon supply.

Risk assets were firm rather than defensive. The S&P 500 rose 0.72%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 1.26%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rebounded 2.17% after two sessions of losses. High-yield and emerging-market debt funds rose modestly, while investment-grade LQD was nearly unchanged. That combination supports a reading of the Treasury move as a policy-timing adjustment, not a flight from growth or credit risk.

## Services Data Shift the Timing, Not the Direction, of Fed Risk

The June services report extended the softer post-payroll tone without showing that the largest part of the U.S. economy was close to contraction. ISM’s headline index declined 0.5 point to 54.0, marking a 24th consecutive month of expansion. Business activity slowed to 55.4 from 57.7, and new orders eased to 55.1 from 57.3. Both remained comfortably above the 50 threshold, indicating that demand continued to grow even as momentum moderated.

Employment provided the principal counterweight to a dovish interpretation. The component rose to 51.2 from 47.9, crossing from contraction into expansion. That improvement does not erase the weak June payroll result, but it adds an independent measure showing that services companies were not uniformly reducing labor demand. For the Fed, the combination is less urgent than strong output, orders and hiring together, yet more resilient than a broad deterioration across all three measures.

Price pressure also remained substantial. The services prices index fell to 67.7 from 71.3, a meaningful decline from May’s elevated level but still a reading consistent with widespread input-cost increases. Supplier deliveries eased to 54.4 from 55.2. The data therefore improved at the margin without providing the kind of low inflation reading that would close the debate over another increase later in 2026.

The supply-chain report strengthened the case that some goods and logistics pressure is receding. The New York Fed’s Global Supply Chain Pressure Index fell to 1.249 in June, or 1.25 standard deviations above its historical average, from a revised 1.810 in May. The index combines transportation costs and manufacturing indicators across seven interconnected economies. Its decline is relevant to producer and goods inflation because it shows less extreme delivery and freight pressure, but its positive level still indicates tighter-than-normal supply conditions.

That distinction helps explain the divergence between real yields and breakevens. The 10-year nominal yield fell 1.5 basis points, while the real yield declined 2.7 basis points and inflation compensation increased 1.2 basis points. Slower services activity and lower logistics pressure reduced the real-rate burden investors required, but improved employment and a still-high services prices index prevented inflation expectations from falling in parallel. Over one month, the 10-year breakeven was still 11.8 basis points lower, reflecting the much larger reversal in energy prices, while the real yield remained 5.7 basis points higher.

Waller’s remarks addressed how the Fed communicates under those mixed conditions rather than which decision it should take next. Speaking at a Bank of Italy conference in Rome, he said forward guidance had helped tighten financial conditions before actual increases during the pandemic-era inflation surge. He also acknowledged that officials had sometimes been too rigid, citing signals in 2020 and 2021 that rates would remain on hold even as inflation accelerated.

His position differed in emphasis from Warsh, who has promised a more data-dependent approach with less reliance on guidance about the future policy path. Waller argued that guidance remains valuable when it does not bind officials to a course that incoming evidence no longer supports. The disagreement matters because the latest data contain precisely the kind of cross-currents that make unconditional signaling hazardous: services demand is slowing, employment breadth improved, logistics pressure eased, and input costs remain high.

The Fed held its target range steady in June, while 9 of 18 officials projected at least one increase this year. Warsh declined to submit a rate forecast. Waller did not use Monday’s appearance to endorse or reject those projections, so his comments should not be treated as another rate signal. They instead preserve an institutional debate over whether conditional communication can influence financial conditions without limiting the Committee’s response to new information.

Market pricing continued to reflect residual tightening risk. Swap traders assigned about a 25% probability to an increase at the next meeting in one intraday account, above the level implied immediately after the weak payroll report but below the roughly one-third probability prevailing before it. Broader currency-market reporting showed traders still expecting at least one Fed increase during 2026. The evidence points to postponement and uncertainty, rather than removal, of the tightening scenario.

Treasury activity was substantial as the market reopened for a full session. FINRA recorded $913.8 billion of par activity across 311,879 trades, 7.7% more than on the shortened July 2 session. Nominal-coupon activity rose 2.6% to $651.6 billion, while TIPS activity increased 13.1% to $17.3 billion. The figures describe two-way turnover rather than investor direction, but they show that the modest rally occurred with activity recovering from the holiday schedule.

Cash demand also absorbed $171 billion of bill supply. Treasury’s $92 billion 91-day bill auction stopped at a 3.735% high rate with a 2.58 bid-to-cover ratio. Competitive tenders totaled $233.813 billion, of which $88.631 billion was accepted; indirect bidders received $42.988 billion, direct bidders $6.841 billion and primary dealers $38.802 billion. The bills settle July 9 and mature October 8.

The $79 billion 182-day sale produced a 3.830% high rate and a 3.05 bid-to-cover ratio. Competitive bids totaled $238.019 billion, with $76.455 billion accepted; indirect bidders received $45.754 billion, directs $7.346 billion and dealers $23.356 billion. Only 0.86% was allotted at the high rate, compared with 93.49% in the 91-day sale. Without when-issued references, the results establish coverage and allocations rather than whether either auction priced through or tailed prevailing levels. They nevertheless showed that large post-holiday bill offerings cleared ahead of July 9 settlement without a visible funding disruption.

## Cheaper Oil Meets Persistent European Pipeline Pressure

The sharp Saudi pricing move deepened the global rates debate because it supplied tangible evidence of excess prompt crude even as central bankers continued to warn about delayed inflation effects. Saudi Aramco lowered the August official selling price for Arab Light delivered to Asia by $11 a barrel, placing it at a $1.50 discount to the regional benchmark. The reduction was the largest monthly cut in at least 26 years and followed the release of barrels that had been trapped or delayed during disruption around the Strait of Hormuz.

The discount was not presented as a new market-share war. Energy analysts attributed it to a temporary overhang as traffic through the strait normalized unevenly and Gulf producers restored flows. Saudi Arabia was also gently raising supply quotas under OPEC+ agreements. The immediate bond implication is disinflationary, but the scale and duration of the effect depend on whether the surplus persists after delayed cargoes clear.

European data showed why lower spot energy does not automatically eliminate pipeline inflation. Euro-area industrial producer prices rose 0.2% in May after a revised 0.7% increase in April, while EU prices also gained 0.2% after a revised 0.8% rise. Euro-area energy prices fell 1.0% on the month, but producer prices excluding energy rose 0.7%. From a year earlier, total euro-area prices were 5.9% higher and ex-energy prices increased 2.8%; energy itself remained 14.0% above its year-earlier level despite the monthly decline.

ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel emphasized that gap between spot relief and the accumulated shock. She said the fragile Middle East peace had helped pull oil down rapidly but had not returned markets to their prewar position, noting that gas prices remained about 40% higher than before the conflict. She also warned that energy inventories still had to be replenished and that core inflation momentum remained stronger than the decline in the headline rate suggested.

Schnabel identified additional risks from Europe’s heat wave, low Rhine water levels and AI investment demand. Her concern was that energy, transportation and supply-chain effects could still reach food, services and wages even if crude remained below its wartime peak. The May producer-price composition lends some support to that qualification: the energy component fell during the month, but non-energy prices continued to rise.

Belgian central-bank Governor Pierre Wunsch offered a less hawkish assessment at the same event. He said the backdrop had become decidedly calmer and that another increase could still be considered, but the disappearance of the original shock without significant second-round effects would not require substantial tightening. He specifically described wage developments as benign. The contrast with Schnabel is now less about whether energy has improved and more about whether the earlier shock has already embedded enough pressure to require another policy response.

Economic activity provided modest offsets to the inflation concern. German real manufacturing orders rose 1.9% in May after April was revised to a 3.2% decline from the initially reported 3.8% fall. The headline was heavily influenced by an 85.0% surge in other transport equipment. Orders excluding large-scale contracts increased 1.0%, a firmer underlying result, although total orders during March through May were still 0.2% lower than in the preceding three months.

The regional split was uneven. Orders from the euro area increased 11.2%, while demand from outside the currency bloc fell 3.2%. The release therefore showed a meaningful rebound with a stronger European component, but not a uniformly accelerating German industrial cycle.

Euro-area retail volume rose 0.2% in May after a revised 0.3% decline in April; EU retail gained 0.5% after a revised 0.6% fall. Euro-area food, drink and tobacco sales increased 0.6%, while non-food sales edged up 0.1%. Automotive-fuel volume fell 0.5% on the month and 4.6% from a year earlier. Total euro-area retail was 1.6% higher than a year before, compared with a 1.9% annual rise across the EU. The pattern was a modest, food-led recovery rather than a broad consumption acceleration.

Those releases leave European duration between two current facts: growth data are no longer uniformly weak, while the inflation impulse is becoming less concentrated in current energy prices. Traders had already reduced expectations for further ECB tightening after the ceasefire and the fall in oil. Schnabel’s warning and firm ex-energy producer prices preserve a case for caution; Wunsch’s focus on benign wages and the vanishing original shock supports waiting for evidence of second-round effects.

## Primary Markets Reward Scale, Reform and Balance-Sheet Repair

Corporate and sovereign borrowers encountered receptive primary markets, but the transactions distinguished between issuers able to demonstrate reform, secured refinancing or strong benchmark demand and those still facing an uneconomic market price.

Welltower increased a planned Canadian-dollar transaction to C$1.15 billion, more than 60% above the minimum C$700 million initially sought. The U.S. senior-housing operator sold C$750 million of 5-year notes and C$400 million of 7-year debt. The longer tranche priced 93 basis points over Canadian government bonds, 2 basis points inside initial discussions, after orders from 36 buyers exceeded three times the tranche size. Proceeds are intended for general corporate purposes, including debt repayment. The deal added to record Canadian-dollar issuance by U.S. borrowers and showed that cross-border demand could support both a larger size and a modest pricing improvement.

Intrum returned to Europe’s high-yield market for the first time since higher financing costs forced the Swedish debt collector into restructuring. The company sought €525 million of senior secured bonds due in 2031, with proceeds intended to redeem euro- and Swedish-krona secured notes due in 2027. Intrum exited U.S. Chapter 11 proceedings last year after rescheduling maturities.

The proposed bond follows a 7.5 billion-krona equity-capital plan intended to accelerate deleveraging by about two years. Intrum said the rights issue portion was fully subscribed and would raise 6 billion kronor before costs. The combination of fresh equity and secured refinancing is materially different from an unsecured return to ordinary financing: the transaction relies on improved capitalization and collateral while pushing out 2027 maturities.

TenneT Germany prepared its first bond issue after the completion of a new ownership structure that includes the German government, Dutch pension capital and sovereign investors. The electricity-grid operator held investor calls for a four-part euro-denominated European Green Bond deal spanning maturities from 4 to 20 years. It plans to invest €67 billion in Germany’s grid, averaging about €13 billion annually from 2026 through 2030, as renewable generation and data-center demand increase the burden on transmission infrastructure.

The German government acquired 25.1% of TenneT Germany, while Dutch pension fund APG, Singapore’s GIC and Norges Bank Investment Management together hold about 46%. Former parent TenneT Holding retains 28.9%. Moody’s rates the company Baa1 with a stable outlook, while S&P and Fitch assign BBB+ stable ratings; the proposed bonds were expected to carry ratings around those levels. The financing arrives after global utility issuance exceeded $337 billion in the first half, showing how grid expansion and power demand are translating into sustained capital-market borrowing.

Hungary completed a €3 billion sovereign sale in its first international issue since Péter Magyar ended Viktor Orbán’s 16-year rule in April. The debt agency sold €1.5 billion each of notes due in 2032 and 2037, attracting combined orders of more than €8 billion. The shorter maturity priced at midswaps plus 80 basis points and the longer at 125 basis points, both 35 basis points tighter than initial indications.

The transaction monetized a convergence rally driven by renewed access to EU funds and the government’s pledge to adopt the euro. Hungary’s existing euro bond due in 2035 had fallen almost 2 percentage points in yield from its March peak to 3.94%. The new administration nevertheless faces a significant budget-deficit overshoot after saying the prior government understated spending. Generali strategist Guillaume Tresca judged that much of the bond rally had already occurred and said Hungary may follow with a dollar issue later this year. Strong execution therefore validated demand for the new political direction without resolving the fiscal work required for euro-area convergence.

Argentina made the opposite financing choice. Economy Minister Luis Caputo said the government did not plan international bond issuance in 2026 or 2027 and would return only if market borrowing became competitive with cheaper alternatives. Fitch and S&P recently raised Argentina to B- from the CCC category, and the spread over Treasuries narrowed by nearly 80 basis points after the June upgrades. Even so, the benchmark 2035 bond still yielded about 8.6%.

Caputo pointed to the 6.3% rate on a $2 billion World Bank-guaranteed facility as a minimum comparison for judging market funding, while declining to identify a precise threshold for issuance. The government intends to rely largely on domestic dollar-denominated placements to cover the remainder of 2026 and roughly $25 billion of dollar debt service next year. It has raised about $4 billion locally this year, expects another $2 billion by year-end and $5 billion in 2027, and recently refinanced a $6 billion repurchase agreement at rates near 7.5%. Officials expect the 2026 financing program to generate a $3.7 billion surplus that can be carried into next year.

Argentina’s objective is to reach investment grade by the end of a possible second Milei term in 2031. Caputo said two of the three major ratings firms regard that path as plausible. The current decision is narrower: recent spread compression improved market access, but not enough to displace guaranteed or domestic alternatives.

Asia’s offshore market supplied a broader structural financing signal. Borrowers in the region issued a record $154 billion equivalent of dollar- and euro-denominated bonds in the quarter ended June 30. Japanese issuers accounted for about 40%, reversing the earlier period when Chinese companies dominated the market. Japanese borrowers sold roughly $62 billion, compared with about $26 billion from Australia and $20 billion from China.

Higher domestic Japanese yields are making foreign-currency issuance attractive when borrowers can swap proceeds back into yen. Euro issuance by Asia-Pacific borrowers increased 63% to a quarterly record of about €37 billion and represented 28% of combined dollar and euro issuance, up from 8% during the prior regional peak in 2021. Citigroup expects issuance across dollars, euros and yen, excluding Japanese domestic deals, to rise about 10% this year to $475 billion. High-grade corporate yields above 5% have sustained demand, although emerging-market Asian investment-grade dollar spreads near 55 basis points leave little cushion against renewed inflation or geopolitical volatility.

## Dollar and Local-Funding Trades Diverge Across Emerging Markets

The dollar’s broader positioning remained much more hawkish than its nearly unchanged July 6 close suggested. Futures wagers on a stronger U.S. currency reached almost $40 billion as of June 30, the largest in more than a decade, after the dollar gained 2% during June. The U.S. Dollar Index ended Monday at 100.85, down less than 0.01% on the day and 0.26% over one week, while remaining 0.78% higher over one month.

The positioning reflects expectations that the Fed may tighten more than other major central banks even after weak payrolls delayed the likely timing. That has made funding choices increasingly important in emerging markets. The dollar’s renewed strength had already eroded some local-currency gains, while another Fed increase would narrow the yield advantage that supported carry positions. The current U.S. data softened the immediate risk but did not remove the underlying rate differential.

The yen presented the clearest expression of that differential. Goldman Sachs revised its 12-month dollar-yen forecast to 165 from 155, citing Japanese fiscal pressure, higher-for-longer Treasury yields and only gradual Bank of Japan increases. It projected 162 in three months and 163 in six months and favored the yen as a funding currency for carry trades. Options markets assigned roughly a 76% probability that dollar-yen would reach 165 by the following June.

Former Japanese currency official Tatsuo Yamasaki argued in the opposite direction, estimating that the yen was at least 10% undervalued and potentially should be near 130 per dollar. He expected further BOJ increases and said even another Fed move would probably be a one-off, limiting further widening in the rate gap. He also warned that Japan’s Finance Ministry had moved beyond verbal warnings and could use small, less visible intervention operations to unsettle short positions, though he regarded coordinated intervention with the U.S. as unlikely.

The dispute captures two different horizons. Current funding economics and relative policy rates continue to favor yen-funded positions, while the scale of undervaluation and intervention risk raises the cost of assuming depreciation will proceed smoothly. The yen was near 162 per dollar around the U.S. close, and hedge funds had built their most bearish stance since 2007.

In the Philippines, Governor Eli Remolona supplied a distinct policy signal by saying the economy could withstand one more 25-basis-point increase. The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas has already raised rates by 50 basis points this year as inflation moved well above its 3% goal. Remolona said another move was possible at the Aug. 27 meeting but indicated that officials were not inclined toward a larger increase while inflation expectations remained anchored.

His growth condition was explicit. Remolona expects activity to rebound in the second half and hopes GDP growth will exceed 3%, supported by a recovery in government spending after scrutiny of public-works projects slowed approvals. June inflation, scheduled after his remarks, was expected to ease to 6.5% from 6.8% in May. The governor’s statement therefore kept a measured increase in play while tying the economy’s capacity to absorb it to stronger fiscal execution and second-half growth.

India’s banking system showed how official funding measures can change domestic issuance without a policy-rate move. Banks sold no certificates of deposit during the three trading sessions through July 2 after raising 708 billion rupees between June 16 and June 29, down from about 1 trillion rupees in the first half of June. The slowdown followed the Reserve Bank of India’s decision to absorb hedging costs for lenders raising dollars overseas, a measure expected to attract more than $50 billion in foreign-currency deposits.

The 1-year CD rate fell to 6.84% from a more than 2-year high of 7.96% in May. Bank treasurers expect issuance to remain subdued through August or September as lenders replace expensive short-term funding with longer-lived foreign-currency deposits. CSB Bank’s Alok Singh said CD rates could decline another 20 to 25 basis points, although aggressive RBI liquidity withdrawal would work in the opposite direction.

Chile provided a longer-duration example of foreign demand responding to currency levels, expected easing and a change in government. Non-resident holdings of peso sovereign bonds rose by a record $2.93 billion in May to $20.2 billion, taking the increase since the start of the year to 36%. The flow followed José Antonio Kast’s election and proposals including corporate-tax reductions, investment guarantees and employment subsidies.

One-year Chilean breakevens had fallen more than 200 basis points since early May to 2.33%, below the central bank’s 3% target. Swaps priced the policy rate at 4.26% in one year, down 40 basis points over the previous month and below the current 4.5% benchmark. Fiscal risk limits the convergence case: the government abandoned its goal of balancing the structural budget by 2030, now targets a 1.5%-of-GDP deficit and requested authority for another $6.2 billion of bond issuance this year. Record foreign inflows reflect improved political and rate expectations, but their durability still depends on delivery of fiscal consolidation.

## Forward Market Significance

The next U.S. session brings May international trade at 08:30 ET on July 7 and the New York Fed’s June Survey of Consumer Expectations at 11:00. Trade flows will update second-quarter growth tracking, while household inflation, labor and credit expectations will test whether lower oil and easing supply-chain pressure are changing the public’s outlook as clearly as they have changed immediate Fed pricing.

Treasury then auctions $90 billion of 42-day bills and $52 billion of 364-day bills at 11:30 ET, followed by a $58 billion 3-year note at 13:00. The coupon sale is the first direct duration-demand test after June payrolls and services data reduced the urgency of a July Fed increase. Its result will need to be judged from the reported stop, when-issued reference and bidder allocations rather than from Monday’s strong bill coverage alone.

The principal policy event is the release of minutes from the June 16–17 FOMC meeting at 14:00 ET on July 8. The account can show how broadly officials supported the shift toward possible 2026 increases, how they weighed inflation against labor resilience, and whether Waller’s preference for flexible guidance had support before Warsh moved to reduce policy signaling. Because the meeting preceded the weak June payroll report and Monday’s services data, the minutes will describe the Committee’s reaction function rather than its response to the latest evidence.

The $39 billion reopening of the 4.375% 10-year note at 13:00 ET that day will test benchmark-duration demand after the 10-year yield fell only 1.5 basis points on July 6 and remained 9.4 basis points higher over one week. The cycle ends July 9 with a $22 billion reopening of the 5.000% 30-year bond. Both coupon issues settle July 15. The 30-year auction is especially important after the long bond barely participated in Monday’s rally and the 2s30s curve steepened to 87.3 basis points.

Initial unemployment claims for the week ended July 4 arrive before the long-bond sale. Holiday effects may make the reading noisy, but claims will provide a timely check on whether the payroll slowdown and improvement in ISM services employment can coexist without a broader increase in layoffs.

Europe’s immediate hard-data test is German industrial production for May on July 7 at 02:00 ET. The release will show whether the 1.9% rebound in factory orders, including the 1.0% gain excluding large contracts, translated into current output. Eurostat’s April services-production report follows at 05:00 ET, adding evidence on the part of the economy most relevant to persistent wage and price pressure.

The Reserve Bank of New Zealand announces its July policy decision at 14:00 NZST on July 8, or 22:00 ET on July 7. Its official cash rate stood at 2.25% after May. The decision is the week’s principal Asia-Pacific rate catalyst and will test how officials balance domestic demand against the global shift toward higher policy paths.

Japan’s next policy evidence comes from BOJ lending and deposit trends and Q1 direct-investment data on July 8, followed by the central bank’s regional economic report on July 9. The regional assessment of activity, wages and prices will bear directly on the disagreement between investors expecting a gradually weaker yen and former officials who believe further BOJ increases can reverse the currency’s undervaluation.

Oil remains the common condition across those decisions. Saudi Arabia’s price cut and restored Hormuz traffic have intensified near-term disinflation, but European producer prices and Schnabel’s warning show that the accumulated shock has not disappeared from non-energy costs. Continued crude oversupply would give central banks more time to distinguish lingering pipeline pressure from durable second-round inflation. A reversal in shipping normalization would quickly restore the imported-price risk that the July 6 Treasury rally only partly removed.

section_summaries.summary: The Treasury rally was modest and concentrated away from the long end as slower services growth, easing logistics pressure and cheaper oil pushed near-term tightening expectations lower. Improving services employment and elevated input costs limited the move, leaving real yields lower, breakevens slightly higher and the curve steeper. Firm equities and modest gains in riskier credit indicated a policy-timing adjustment rather than defensive demand.

section_summaries.market_read: Falling real yields alongside higher breakevens showed relief on the real-rate burden without comparable confidence on inflation.
section_summaries.section_title: Services Data Shift the Timing, Not the Direction, of Fed Risk
section_summaries.summary: June ISM services slowed to 54.0, but activity and new orders remained in expansion, employment rebounded to 51.2 and the prices index stayed high at 67.7. Supply-chain pressure eased but remained above normal. That mix lowered real yields without pulling breakevens down and postponed rather than removed tightening risk. Waller defended flexible forward guidance without giving a new rate signal, while traders continued to price residual risk of at least one 2026 increase.

section_summaries.market_read: Spot oil relief is disinflationary, but rising ex-energy producer prices leave Europe’s pipeline inflation unresolved.
section_summaries.section_title: Cheaper Oil Meets Persistent European Pipeline Pressure
section_summaries.summary: Saudi Aramco cut August Arab Light pricing for Asia by $11 a barrel as delayed Hormuz cargoes returned, adding a strong near-term disinflation signal. Europe’s May producer data showed the limit: energy prices fell 1.0%, but prices excluding energy rose 0.7%. Schnabel warned that accumulated energy and supply-chain effects could persist, while Wunsch emphasized calmer conditions and benign wages. German orders and euro-area retail improved, but neither showed a broad acceleration.

section_summaries.market_read: Recent spread compression improved Argentina’s access, but external funding remained uncompetitive with guaranteed and domestic alternatives.
section_summaries.section_title: Primary Markets Reward Scale, Reform and Balance-Sheet Repair
section_summaries.summary: Primary markets were receptive when borrowers paired issuance with scale, reform, collateral or strategic investment. Welltower increased its Canadian-dollar deal to C$1.15 billion; Intrum paired €525 million of secured refinancing with fresh equity; TenneT Germany prepared a 4-part green issue after its ownership reset; and Hungary drew more than €8 billion for a €3 billion sale after its political turn. Argentina still rejected external bonds at an 8.6% benchmark yield, while Asia-Pacific offshore issuance reached a quarterly record led by Japan.

section_summaries.market_read: Relative policy rates still favor dollar strength and yen funding, while official measures are redirecting local funding in India.
section_summaries.next_check: The Philippines’ Aug. 27 decision will test whether anchored expectations and stronger H2 growth allow another 25-basis-point increase.
section_summaries.section_title: Dollar and Local-Funding Trades Diverge Across Emerging Markets
section_summaries.summary: The dollar closed nearly unchanged but remained supported by almost $40 billion of bullish futures positioning and expectations of wider policy-rate differentials. Yen-funded carry remained attractive, although undervaluation and intervention risk challenged forecasts for further depreciation. The Philippines kept one more 25-basis-point increase in play, India’s support for offshore funding reduced bank CD issuance and rates, and record foreign demand for Chilean peso bonds remained conditional on fiscal consolidation.

July 7 brings U.S. trade, household expectations and the first coupon auction after softer payrolls and services data. The July 8 FOMC minutes will clarify support for possible 2026 increases and flexible guidance, while the reopened 10-year and July 9 long-bond sale will test duration demand after the curve steepened. German output, the RBNZ decision and BOJ evidence broaden the policy calendar, but sustained oil oversupply or renewed Hormuz disruption remains the common inflation condition.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries rally modestly as softer services delay Fed risk, while the long end lags
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries ended July 6 with a modest rally concentrated in shorter and intermediate maturities. The 2-year yield fell 2.6 basis points to 4.112%, the 5-year declined 3 basis points to 4.201% and the 10-year eased 1.5 basis points to 4.47%, while the 30-year was almost unchanged at 4.985%. The 2s10s curve steepened to 35.8 basis points and 2s30s to 87.3 basis points. The 10-year real yield fell 2.7 basis points, but the breakeven rose 1.2 basis points, showing that the rally reflected lower real-rate pressure rather than a broad retreat in inflation compensation.

June ISM services slowed to 54.0 as business activity and new orders moderated, while the New York Fed’s supply-chain index fell to 1.25 standard deviations above its historical average. Employment returned to expansion and the services prices index remained elevated at 67.7, preserving the possibility of another Fed increase later in 2026 even as weak payrolls and softer activity reduced the urgency of a July move. Saudi Aramco’s unusually large August price cut and the monthly collapse in crude prices added a stronger near-term disinflation signal, although persistent services costs and European non-energy producer inflation kept the longer end cautious.

Equities advanced, led by technology and semiconductors, while high-yield and emerging-market debt firmed and investment-grade credit was nearly unchanged. That mix supports a policy-timing adjustment rather than a flight from growth or credit risk. Primary markets were also receptive to borrowers offering scale, reform, secured refinancing or strategic investment, while Argentina judged external borrowing still too expensive despite recent spread compression.
overall_summary.summary: Softer services activity, easing supply-chain stress and cheaper oil lowered near-term Fed urgency and pulled short and intermediate Treasury yields down, but stronger services employment, elevated input costs and lingering inflation uncertainty left the long end nearly unchanged and steepened the curve.
